output.brief: The overrun is mostly not caused by the hiring freeze. Regular holdover overtime hours rose only 1.5% (the rest of that line is the July wage increase). Call-back pay rose from $38k to $289k. About 1,960 of the call-backs are closing duties that started on 1 April, when the closing contract lapsed and maintenance staff took over nightly closing on 3-hour-minimum call-backs. They appear only in the three districts that lost the contract. Summit Hill kept its contract and barely moved. Eastgate has one vacancy and a near-doubled bill. Internal Audit matched the claims against lock logs and found no padding, so the hotline allegation is not supported. Weather is not a main driver. The July vacancy correlation is just two things that happened to rise together. Next steps: restore contracted closing for the 41 sites (or re-tender), and track call-back spending against the April–September level. Don't cap overtime, because crews would stop taking call-backs and the closing, which liability coverage requires, wouldn't get done. Don't discipline anyone yet. Fairness of Eastgate call-back allocation is unproven, since the sign-up sheets were discarded. Start keeping those records and review how call-backs are spread. Injury-claim links to overtime remain unproven, so match claims to payroll hours. The vacancy exemption isn't justified by this evidence. Confidence is fairly high.
